blocks.title: Faces & Products
blocks.what: Reuse the same face or product in every shot, and get several angles of it.
say: Save this as a reusable reference called 'the bottle', then use it in three shots: on a kitchen counter, held in a hand, on a store shelf.
I want a spokesperson who looks the same in every ad. Here are 12 photos. Train a proper identity from these.
Using 'the bottle', give me three product shots: profile, straight-on, and 45-degree. Same studio lighting in all three.
mistakes: Two trained identities in one shot. Only one is allowed per generation. Use two saved references instead.
Skipping training for a recurring brand face, then seeing it drift between ads.
Expecting three angles from one request. It is three separate generations.
Looking for an all-purpose swap tool. Wardrobe and material swaps are the try-on format.
blocks.try: Save a reference from one product photo. Generate it in two different settings and compare.
blocks.under: Saved reference = Reference Element (show_reference_elements). Trained identity = Soul (show_characters, soul_2 / soul_cinematic), 5 to 20 photos, about ten minutes, one per generation. Each angle = a separate generate_image call with the same Element id. Wearable swaps = ugc_virtual_try_on.

blocks.title: Cinema Studio
blocks.what: Brief a shot like a director. Real lens and light words, not software settings.
say: Give me a wide, noir-toned establishing shot: anamorphic lens feel, shallow depth of field, high-contrast rim lighting, slow dolly-in toward the subject. Prioritize quality over speed.
mistakes: Asking for a 30-second shot in one go. One generation tops out around 12 to 15 seconds. Chain shots.
Describing a move in distances ("three feet left") instead of cinema words ("slow lateral tracking shot").
blocks.try: Describe one shot with two light or lens phrases and one genre word. Compare it with "make it look nice".
blocks.under: cinematic_studio_video_v2 or cinematic_studio_3_0. Real parameters: genre, mode (pro / std), speedramp. Lens and light live only in the prompt text. There is no numeric camera-path or f-stop field.

blocks.title: Marketing Studio
blocks.what: Real product photo or website in, finished on-brand ad out. The product stays locked.
say: Here's our site: [url]. Pull our brand colors and build an unboxing-style ad for [product], vertical for TikTok, in a bright, energetic setting.
mistakes: Expecting the hook and setting dials on every format. They work on five: UGC, Tutorial, Unboxing, Product Review, Virtual Try-On.
Calling a whole website or app a "product". Say "webproduct" when there is no single item.
blocks.try: Give Claude your site link and ask it to pull the brand colors first. Check they match.
blocks.under: show_marketing_studio (brand_kit, product / webproduct) feeds generate_video with model marketing_studio_video, product_ids and a mode slug (ugc_unboxing, tv_spot, product_showcase and about 20 more).

blocks.title: Motion transfer
blocks.what: Make a still image move the way something in another video moves.
say: [photo] [video of a dance move] Make my character do the motion from this video.
Swap the [object] in this video for the one in this image.
mistakes: A driving video with a very different body type or framing. The closer the match, the cleaner the result.
Mixing it up with voice and lip-sync. One moves the body, the other matches audio.
blocks.try: Pick a still and a short clip of one clear motion. Transfer it.
blocks.under: motion_control (Kling 3.0), or Genjutsu: hf_mult_motion_control (copy motion), hf_mult_replace_object (swap an object).

blocks.title: Voice & dubbing
blocks.what: One consistent voice, any of 18 languages, timed to the picture.
say: Give this video a calm, confident female voice reading: '[your line]', timed to match the video.
Swap the voice in this clip for something deeper and older.
mistakes: Expecting dubbing to translate on-screen text. It only handles spoken audio.
Asking for a language outside the 18 supported.
blocks.try: Add one line of dialogue to a finished video, in a voice you describe in your own words.
blocks.under: list_voices, generate_audio (seed_audio), sync_so for retiming (bounce / loop / cut_off / silence / remap), dubbing, voice_change, narrator workflow for a full voiceover.

blocks.title: Finish
blocks.what: Sharper, cleaner, and the right shape for each platform.
say: Cut the background out of this product shot.
I need this video in 9:16 and 1:1 for two platforms.
mistakes: Upscaling a soft or bad generation. Upscale sharpens detail, it does not fix a bad take. Re-generate first.
Forgetting file type before publishing (see Publish).
blocks.try: Take a favorite image to a 4K upscale and a background-free cutout.
blocks.under: upscale_image / upscale_video, remove_background, outpaint_image, reframe. Some small finishing tools skip the cost preview; ask Claude to check your balance before and after.

blocks.title: Publish & check
blocks.what: Get an honest read before posting, then post.
say: Before we publish, check how this is likely to perform and tell me the weakest part.
Post this to my TikTok. Ask me anything you need to before it goes live.
mistakes: Posting a PNG as a photo. TikTok photos need JPEG or WebP. Convert first.
Not choosing privacy and comment settings ahead of time.
Treating a virality score as a promise. It is a direction, not a guarantee.
blocks.try: Run a performance check on your best clip. Fix the one weakest thing it flags.
blocks.under: virality_predictor for the read. tiktok_* tools for connect and publish; TikTok requires privacy, captions and disclosure choices before anything goes live.

All scenes are done and approved. Now assemble them into one cinematic scroll experience that works like a website. Read START-HERE.md, docs/AE-route.md and ce-04 (spectacular tier) first. Work in EXPLORE mode.

**What I have:** [folder path with the scene clips, locked element images, real logo and pack files, music if any]
**Goal:** the page scrolls like a film. Scroll down = the film plays forward. Scroll up = it plays back. Text and the product appear at the right moments.

**Step 1. Plan (show me, then stop).** One table, one row per scroll section: section | which scene clip | what the viewer reads (headline/line, in code) | how it hands off to the next (match cut, push through steam, whip). Include the order and total scroll length. Wait for my yes.

**Step 2. After Effects (the film).**
- Import the real clips, logo and pack files. Never redraw them.
- One comp at 1920x1080, 30 fps. Cut each scene to its best seconds. Trim half a second off both ends.
- Build the hand-offs between scenes as transitions through a real object in frame.
- One grade across all scenes. Fix mismatches.
- Add the real logo and pack shot at the end. Text comes from real fonts, set in AE or left to the page (tell me which).
- Render a frame from every scene and check each one against the real files before moving on.
- Export: (a) a frame sequence, WebP, 1280 wide for desktop and 720 wide for phone, about 24 frames per second of film; (b) one MP4 backup. Tell me file sizes.

**Step 3. The page (the scroll).**
- One HTML page. GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Lenis. The frame sequence plays on a canvas, scrubbed by scroll position. Preload the first frames first, load the rest in the background.
- Headlines and the call to action are real text on top, fading in at set scroll points. One main button.
- Phone: use the 720 sequence. Show a poster frame while loading. Respect reduced motion (show stills, no scrubbing).
- Pause everything when the page is off screen.

**Step 4. Show me.** Give me a local preview link and a phone-width screenshot of 5 moments (start, 3 middle, end). Say the total weight in MB and how long a first load takes. List anything that looks wrong and how you would fix it. Do not publish or touch any live site.
